brandStory: Benda motorcycles are built by Hangzhou Saturn Power Technology Co., Ltd., a company established in 2016 that now runs two factories, one in the north and one in the south. It has its own digital simulation and analysis team and designs and builds engines, two-wheelers and four-wheel vehicles, with a range centred on V-twin and V4 cruisers.

models.name: LFC 700
models.tagline: 676 cc four-cylinder power cruiser with Brembo brakes and 310 mm tyre
summary: The Benda LFC 700 is a power cruiser built around a 676 cc liquid-cooled four-cylinder engine with 16 valves and twin overhead camshafts, rated at 84.48 hp and 60 Nm. It sits on an aluminium frame with a single-sided swingarm and a 310 mm wide rear tyre, which gives it a low, muscular stance that is hard to miss on a showroom floor.

Braking is by Brembo, with twin 320 mm floating front discs and four-piston calipers, backed by ABS. KYB supplies the 43 mm upside-down fork and the adjustable rear shock. A 5-inch colour TFT display, selectable riding modes, a slipper clutch and a 17-litre tank complete a package aimed at riders stepping up to a large four-cylinder cruiser.

models.name: LFC 700 Pro
models.tagline: Four-cylinder cruiser with air suspension and 650–730 mm seat height
summary: The Benda LFC 700 Pro takes the 676 cc liquid-cooled inline four of the LFC 700 and adds a dual-chamber rear air suspension that can be adjusted electronically. Riders can lower the bike for a low, aggressive stance or raise it for comfort, and the seat height moves between 650 and 730 mm, which widens the range of customers who can ride it.

Output is 77.78 hp and 60 Nm, fed by Bosch fuel injection with a ram-air intake built into the headlamp. Brembo calipers on twin 320 mm floating discs, Bosch dual-channel ABS, a 300 mm rear tyre on a single-sided swingarm and quad exhaust tips complete the hardware, while a 5-inch TFT links to the B-ConnecteD app for ride tracking and navigation.

models.name: Chinchilla 500
models.tagline: 475.6 cc V-twin cruiser with belt drive, ABS and traction control
summary: The Benda Chinchilla 500 is a mid-size cruiser powered by a 475.6 cc liquid-cooled V-twin with eight valves, producing 46.94 hp and 42 Nm. Drive goes through a six-speed gearbox with a slipper clutch to a belt final drive, so there is no chain to clean or adjust. At 215 kg with a 705 mm seat, it suits riders moving up from smaller cruisers.

Wide 16-inch tyres, 150 mm at the front and 180 mm at the rear, give it a heavyweight look. A 41 mm upside-down fork, twin preload-adjustable rear shocks and a 320 mm floating front disc with a four-piston caliper handle the chassis side, with ABS and traction control fitted. The 16-litre tank, stainless steel exhausts and LED lights finish it off.

summary: The Benda Chinchilla 250 pairs a 249 cc liquid-cooled V-twin with a CVT automatic gearbox and belt final drive, so there is no clutch lever and no gear changing. It makes 25.84 CV and 25 Nm, and with a 690 mm seat, high handlebars and a 192 kg kerb weight it is aimed at new and returning riders who want a cruiser that is easy to live with.

Rider aids are fitted as standard: dual-channel ABS and traction control, with a 320 mm front disc and four-piston caliper. A 37 mm upside-down fork and twin preload-adjustable shocks handle the suspension. Full LED lighting with a round headlight, a round digital display showing speed, gear position and fuel, plus USB-A and USB-C charging complete the specification.

Rated at 33.5 hp and 31 Nm, with strong pulling power at low and middle revs, it handles town traffic without any clutch work and still has enough in reserve for open-road cruising at up to 129 km/h.

Styling leans on classic cues: a round LED headlight with a chrome halo ring that works as a daytime running light, a round LCD display, chromed twin rear shocks and twin stainless steel silencers. Underneath sit a 37 mm upside-down fork, a 320 mm front disc with Bosch dual-channel ABS, traction control and a 16-litre tank, with a 690 mm seat.

models.name: Darkflag 500
models.tagline: 496 cc V4 cruiser with cruise control and electronic air suspension
summary: The Benda Darkflag 500 is a cruiser built around a 496 cc liquid-cooled V4 engine with 16 valves, producing 46.94 hp and 42 Nm. It uses a ride-by-wire throttle and shuts down its rear two cylinders at idle to cut fuel use and heat. Power reaches the rear wheel through a six-speed gearbox, a slipper clutch and a belt final drive.

Touring comfort is built in. Cruise control, traction control and ABS are fitted, and an electronically adjusted rear air suspension sets ride height between 670 and 700 mm. The seat is shaped for two people, and the cockpit uses a floating central instrument, backlit switches and an LED fuel gauge on the tank. Kerb weight is 260 kg with a 16-litre tank.

A 15-litre tank, LED instruments, 158 mm of ground clearance and a top speed of 120 km/h round out a practical first cruiser.
